title: Console widget: Throughput SLO status (floor adherence + recent incidents/credits)
creator: Lauren Bishop
description:
## Summary
Design exploration for an in-console widget that summarizes a Dedicated deployment’s throughput SLO status: (1) whether the committed throughput floor is being met (per SLO semantics) and (2) recent incidents and any resulting service credits.

This widget is intended to reduce confusion during escalations (“are we currently below the committed floor?”), help CS/Sales answer common questions quickly, and give customers a clear, non-alarming view of current SLO health.

---

## Goals
- Provide an at-a-glance status for **Committed Throughput Floor** adherence for a Dedicated deployment.
- Make it easy to drill into: time window, measurement details, and what is / isn’t included.
- Show a lightweight history of **recent SLO-related incidents** and **credits** (if applicable), with links to details.
- Support tier-aware messaging (Standard / Plus / Premium), without exposing internal-only fleet signals.

## Non-goals
- Replace the full Dedicated dashboard (deep perf analysis stays in dashboards).
- Provide real-time debugging tools (no per-request traces in this widget).
- Promise “instant remediation” (widget should not imply guaranteed immediate recovery).

---

## Primary users / use cases
1) **Dedicated customer admin / ML eng**
   - “Are we meeting our committed throughput right now?”
   - “Did Redwood acknowledge an issue? Is there an incident I can reference internally?”

2) **CS / Support** (internal console view)
   - Quick snapshot during ticket triage.
   - Confirm whether customer is eligible for credits and whether a credit has been applied.

3) **Sales / Solutions**
   - During renewal / expansion: show how commitments are measured and reported.

---

## Placement (proposed)
- Dedicated Deployment details page (Console)
  - Above the fold, right rail or top summary row alongside: Tier, Region, Model pinned, Current utilization.
- Optional: surface as a compact tile in a Dedicated “Deployments” list view (status only + tooltip).

---

## Widget content (v1)
### A) Header
- Title: **Throughput SLO status**
- Pill: Status (Green/Yellow/Red/Gray)

Status definitions (UX-level)
- **Healthy (Green):** currently meeting floor and within error budget.
- **At risk (Yellow):** burn-rate elevated / risk of breach in the rolling window.
- **Breached (Red):** SLO breach detected (per SLO evaluator).
- **Unavailable (Gray):** insufficient data / metrics delayed / deployment newly provisioned / permissions.

Note: Final mapping depends on SRE burn-rate alert thresholds + evaluator output. Design should not directly reference “burn rate” unless we can explain it simply.

### B) Primary metric line
- **Committed floor:** e.g., “≥ 18k tok/s (P50 over 5-min windows)” (exact wording TBD per PM-503)
- **Current measured:** e.g., “Now: 19.2k tok/s” (optional; see “Customer vs internal view”)

If we only show a status, we should still display committed floor value for transparency.

### C) Time window + measurement details (inline)
- Small text: “Measured over rolling 30 days. Updates every ~5 minutes.” (exact window TBD; align with SLO doc)
- “How we measure” link opens a drawer/modal with:
  - Metric definition summary (tokens/sec attribution)
  - Exclusions summary (customer throttling, unsupported model/version, etc.)
  - Known caveats (streaming accounting; batching/caching effects) in customer-friendly language

### D) Mini trend
- Sparkline for last 24h / 7d showing floor line + measured throughput (simple)
- Hover/tap reveals timestamps and values

### E) Recent incidents & credits
- “Recent SLO events” list (last 30/90 days; likely 3 most recent)
  - Incident title + date range + status (Resolved/Investigating)
  - Link: “View incident details” (status page entry or in-console incident detail)
- “Credits” section (only if applicable)
  - “Service credit applied: $X (Invoice YYYY-MM)” or “Credit pending review”
  - Link: “View credit details” (internal-only initially; customer view may show summary only)

---

## Views & permissions
We likely need two variants:
1) **Customer-facing view** (default for customer org users)
   - Conservative details: status + committed floor + high-level trend + public incident references.
   - Avoid internal annotations like saturation, queue depth, “node drain,” or region-level capacity constraints.

2) **Internal view** (CS/Sales/Solutions)
   - Includes “Current measured throughput” and quick links to dashboards/runbooks.
   - May include an internal-only callout: “Top contributing factor” (if we can classify safely) e.g., “Model pinned to non-recommended ctx” vs “Infra incident.”

Permission handling:
- If user lacks access to incident details: show list item titles but link gated.
- If credit details are internal-only: customer sees “If a credit is applied, it will appear on your next invoice” + a support CTA.

---

## States (wireframe-level)
1) **Healthy**
- Green pill “Healthy”
- Copy: “Meeting committed floor”
- Sparkline above floor line

2) **At risk**
- Yellow pill “At risk”
- Copy: “Throughput trending below commitment in the current window.”
- CTA: “Contact support” (if customer) / “Open escalation playbook” (internal)

3) **Breached**
- Red pill “Breached”
- Copy: “Committed throughput floor not met in the rolling window.”
- Show incident banner if there is an active incident tied to this deployment.

4) **Insufficient data / warming up**
- Gray pill “Collecting data”
- Copy options:
  - “New deployment—SLO reporting begins after the initial warm-up period.”
  - “Metrics delayed—status will update shortly.”

5) **Misconfiguration / excluded scenario** (careful)
- Prefer neutral language:
  - “Not currently eligible for SLO reporting” with explanation (e.g., unsupported model/version pinned)
- Must align with contract language; avoid implying customer fault.

---

## Copy / terminology guidelines (draft)
- Use “Committed throughput floor” (not “guarantee”) unless Legal/PM confirms.
- Avoid “tokens/sec” if we can’t explain it; but Dedicated buyers are technical—likely OK with tooltip.
- Always include a “Learn more” link to the Dedicated SLO doc / FAQ.

Proposed microcopy
- Tooltip on committed floor: “This is the minimum throughput Redwood commits to deliver under the Dedicated Throughput SLO, measured per the policy.”
- Tooltip on sparkline: “Measured throughput over time. The dashed line indicates your committed floor.”

---

## Data requirements (design-facing)
Inputs we need from Eng/Obs:
- deployment_id → tier, region, shape (for display context)
- SLO evaluator output:
  - current_state: healthy/at_risk/breached/no_data
  - compliance over window (boolean + %)
  - current measured throughput (optional)
  - last_updated timestamp
- Incident feed:
  - incidents linked to deployment_id (or region/pool + affected deployments mapping)
- Credits feed:
  - credit status + amount + invoice reference, associated to deployment or account

Open question: do we have a single source of truth for incidents/credits that’s safe to show customers? If not, V1 might only link to our status page + show “contact support for billing adjustments.”

---

## Open questions / decisions needed
1) **Metric naming & units**
   - “tok/s” vs “tokens/sec” vs “throughput units” (PM prefers explicit tokens/sec; confirm).

2) **Time window shown in UI**
   - SRE doc suggests rolling window + 5-min aggregation; confirm what we can present simply.

3) **At risk state semantics**
   - Can we reliably compute “at risk” without alert noise? (See early alert tuning threads.)

4) **Customer visibility into credits**
   - Do we show credit amounts? Or only “credit applied” status?

5) **Multi-deployment accounts**
   - Widget is per-deployment, but customers may expect an account-level rollup. Out of scope for V1.

6) **Streaming accounting edge cases**
   - We need to ensure values match what customers see elsewhere (avoid repeating the streaming double-counting mismatch incident).

---

## Proposed next steps
- Create two wireframe options:
  - Option A: compact tile + drilldown drawer
  - Option B: expanded card with sparkline + incidents inline
- Review with:
  - Product (Lauren Bishop)
  - SRE (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes)
  - Observability (Allison Grant / Sergio Costa)
  - Support/CS (Dev Patel / Rachel Kim)
- After decision, handoff spec to Console team under DES-771 for implementation.

comments: 2025-02-13 (Allison Grant): Strong preference for a simple state model in the widget (Healthy/At risk/Breached/No data). Avoid exposing internal saturation panels to customers; keep those behind a link for internal viewers.

2025-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): If we show “At risk,” we need a deterministic rule from the evaluator; otherwise it will create support churn. Suggest mapping “At risk” only when fast burn-rate alert would fire (internal), and keep customer view binary (Healthy/Breached) for v1.

2025-02-21 (Dev Patel): Please include a prominent link to the escalation playbook for internal users and a “Contact support” CTA for customers. Also include last-updated timestamp so support can rule out stale metrics quickly.

2025-02-25 (Lauren Bishop): Customer view must align with contract language—avoid the word “guarantee.” We should still show committed floor value and a clear explanation of exclusions via the “How we measure” drawer.

2025-02-27 (Sergio Costa): We can provide a sparkline dataset at 5-min resolution (24h) and hourly (7d/30d). Incident linking by deployment_id may lag; for v1 we might only have region/pool → affected deployments mapping.
